No tiene ningún impacto en las convenciones de nomenclatura canadienses ni en la forma en que el resto del mundo se refiere al lago. "Dado que actualizamos Google Maps para reflejar los cambios de nombre en las fuentes oficiales del Gobierno —que en el caso de Estados Unidos es el GNIS—, los usuarios de Maps en Estados Unidos verán 'lago América', los de Canadá seguirán viendo 'lago Ontario' y los que se encuentren fuera de Estados Unidos y Canadá verán ambos nombres", afirmó Google en una entrada de blog publicada el sábado. La Casa Blanca, la oficina del primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, y la del primer ministro de Ontario, Doug Ford no hicieron comentarios inmediatos el domingo sobre la decisión de Google. Google Maps realizó un cambio similar con el golfo de México el año pasado, denominándolo "golfo de América" tras el decreto ejecutivo de Trump, en su primer día en el cargo, por el que se cambiaba el nombre de esa masa de agua. Carney rechazó el jueves el cambio de nombre del lago. La gobernadora demócrata de Nueva York, Kathy Hochul, cuyo estado comparte una extensa frontera con Canadá, declaró que "Nueva York no lo llamará así", mientras que Phil Scott, el gobernador republicano del vecino estado de Vermont, calificó la decisión de Trump de "mezquina y decepcionante" en las redes sociales. Ford inauguró el sábado un gran cartel a orillas del lago en el que se lee: "Lago Ontario: ahora y siempre", tanto en inglés como en francés. "El presidente Trump puede llamarlo como quiera, pero les puedo asegurar que el resto del mundo siempre lo llamará lago Ontario", comentó.

item.title: Rashford to make first Man United start since 2024 against Ipswich
item.description: Marcus Rashford is set to make his first Manchester United start for over 18 months when Michael Carrick's side host Ipswich Town in the Premier League on Sunday looking to respond to their shock opening-day defeat by Hull City.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Marcus Rashford is set to make his first Manchester United start for over 18 months when Michael Carrick's side host Ipswich Town in the Premier League on Sunday looking to respond to their shock opening-day defeat by Hull City. The England forward has endured a turbulent period since he fell out of favour with former United manager Ruben Amorim and had loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona. The 28-year-old Rashford, who was in the England squad at this year's World Cup, made his first appearance for United since December 2024 as a substitute in the loss to Hull.

item.title: Naufragio de transbordador deja siete muertos y más de 20 desaparecidos frente a costas de Chipre
item.description: Al menos siete personas fallecieron y 23 quedaron en paradero desconocido después de que un transbordador que transportaba a unos 270 pasajeros y tripulantes volcara el domingo frente a las costas del norte de Chipre, dejando a los sobrevivientes aferrados al casco volcado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Al menos siete personas fallecieron y 23 quedaron en paradero desconocido después de que un transbordador que transportaba a unos 270 pasajeros y tripulantes volcara el domingo frente a las costas del norte de Chipre, dejando a los sobrevivientes aferrados al casco volcado. El transbordador, de propiedad privada, zarpó del puerto de Kyrenia a las 12:30 hora local (0930 GMT) y, según las autoridades, comenzó a hacer agua de inmediato por causas desconocidas. Se dirigía al puerto turco de Tasucu, en la provincia de Mersin, en el Mediterráneo oriental. La tragedia se produjo frente a la costa de Kyrenia, un popular destino vacacional tanto para los lugareños como para los turistas. El transbordador implicado, un catamarán, era uno de los varios servicios marítimos que conectan a diario el norte de Chipre con Turquía. El líder turcochipriota, Tufan Erhurman, afirmó que se había rescatado con vida a 237 personas, mientras que siete habían fallecido y aún se buscaba a otras 23. "Hemos rescatado a 237 personas con vida. Sin embargo, también hemos recuperado los cuerpos de siete personas que perdieron la vida. Estamos profundamente entristecidos por ello", declaró Erhurman a CNN Turk en una transmisión en directo. Las imágenes de video mostraban a personas con chalecos salvavidas rojos sentadas o de pie sobre la embarcación volcada, mientras las autoridades movilizaban a la guardia costera y a embarcaciones privadas para que les ayudaran a llegar a la costa. "Aún no hemos podido localizar a 23 personas. Los equipos de búsqueda y rescate están trabajando intensamente para encontrarlas", afirmó Erhurman. "Si hay personas dentro de la embarcación, llegar hasta ellas no parece fácil por el momento. También se están realizando esfuerzos usando otras tecnologías para localizarlas". Chipre se vio azotado el sábado por fuertes tormentas, en las que una persona falleció después de que su velero se estrellara contra las rocas en un mar embravecido al sureste de la isla. Al ser preguntado sobre la causa del vuelco, Erhurman se refirió a la tormenta del sábado, pero afirmó que las condiciones meteorológicas se consideraban adecuadas para navegar. "Aquí reina una gran conmoción. No es algo que hayamos vivido antes (…) estamos profundamente entristecidos. Todo el mundo está haciendo todo lo que puede y poniendo todo su empeño", afirmó desde el centro de crisis habilitado en la zona. El primer ministro turcochipriota, Unal Ustel, afirmó que se estaba llevando a cabo una importante operación de rescate. "Nuestra única prioridad en estos momentos es la vida humana. Todas las instituciones de nuestro Estado, nuestras fuerzas de seguridad, equipos sanitarios y efectivos de búsqueda y rescate están sobre el terreno, coordinándose plenamente", declaró a los periodistas tras presidir una reunión del comité de gestión de crisis. El Ministerio del Interior turcochipriota informó de que el transbordador de pasajeros "FILOJET" transportaba a 259 pasajeros y ocho tripulantes, y que comenzó a hacer agua a unas cuatro millas náuticas de Kyrenia mientras navegaba de Kyrenia a Tasucu, en Turquía. Según el comunicado del ministerio, se desplegaron en el lugar cuatro embarcaciones de la guardia costera turcochipriota y un barco civil de pasajeros, junto con cinco embarcaciones de la guardia costera turca y dos helicópteros.

item.title: NATO sees no imminent threat of attack, official says
item.description: A NATO official said on Sunday Russia is stepping up hybrid acts in Europe, but that at this time the alliance sees no imminent threat of attack.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A NATO official said on Sunday Russia is stepping up hybrid acts in Europe, but that at this time the alliance sees no imminent threat of attack. "Even as the Russians are facing very substantial resistance from Ukraine, they are stepping up attacks on Ukraine as well as hybrid acts in Europe," the official said. "As always, NATO remains vigilant and alert to the variety of threats we face. At this time, we see no imminent threat of attack," the official said, adding: "We continue to stand with Ukraine. And NATO continues to work around the clock to keep our one billion people safe". Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Saturday that Poland and NATO must be prepared for various scenarios, and that a provocation by Russia against any NATO member cannot be ruled out. CIA Director John Ratcliffe flew to Russia on Tuesday to meet briefly with intelligence counterparts. Two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters that Ratcliffe [USN:L1N44O0Y1 TEXT:"brought up"] the possibility of a Russian operation against a NATO member during that meeting, though it was unclear if that was the sole purpose of the trip. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Tuesday that the German government will soon announce who is responsible for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport earlier this month. Russia has consistently denied any involvement in sabotage planning or attacks on Europe, and rejects such accusations as Western scaremongering.

item.title: Trump says US will refill Strategic Petroleum Reserve using Venezuelan oil
item.description: He called it a "Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States."
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday that oil from a recently struck deal with Venezuela will be used to replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which has been drawn down sharply in recent years to respond to global supply disruptions and high fuel prices. Trump said in a social media post that the "topping out" process will begin shortly, describing the Venezuelan oil as a “Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States.” It is unclear how quickly the Venezuela deal could provide oil for the reserve or deliver any near-term benefit to U.S. motorists. The agreement Trump [USN:L6N44P14L TEXT:"announced on Friday"] is aimed at reviving Venezuela's battered oil industry, but it will require significant investment and infrastructure work before production can rise substantially. The reserve held about 290 million barrels as of August 21, near a 44-year low, after the United States drew down its stockpile under both the Biden and Trump administrations in response to global supply disruptions, including Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the conflict with Iran.

item.title: Trump dice que EEUU repondrá su Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo con crudo venezolano
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó el domingo que el crudo procedente de un acuerdo alcanzado recientemente con Venezuela se utilizará para reponer la Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo del país.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó el domingo que el crudo procedente de un acuerdo alcanzado recientemente con Venezuela se utilizará para reponer la Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo del país. Esta reserva se ha reducido de forma drástica en los últimos años para hacer frente a las interrupciones del suministro mundial y a los elevados precios del combustible. Trump señaló en una publicación en las redes sociales que el proceso de "llenado" comenzará en breve, y describió el petróleo venezolano como un "regalo de Venezuela al pueblo de Estados Unidos". No está claro con qué rapidez el acuerdo con Venezuela podrá aportar petróleo a la reserva ni si reportará algún beneficio a corto plazo a los estadounidenses. El acuerdo que Trump anunció el viernes tiene como objetivo reactivar la maltrecha industria petrolera venezolana, pero requerirá una inversión significativa y obras de infraestructura antes de que la producción pueda aumentar de forma sustancial. La reserva contaba con unos 290 millones de barriles a 21 de agosto, cerca de su mínimo en 44 años. Estados Unidos redujo sus reservas tanto bajo el Gobierno de Joe Biden como el de Trump en respuesta a las interrupciones en el suministro mundial causado, entre otros, por la invasión rusa de Ucrania y el conflicto con Irán.

item.title: Federación de Países Bajos pide reforma integral de la FIFA y propone cumbre mundial en Ámsterdam
item.description: La Federación de Fútbol de Países Bajos (KNVB) anunció que quiere organizar una cumbre internacional en Ámsterdam para reformar por completo la FIFA, al tiempo que pidió que el presidente Gianni Infantino sea sustituido antes de 2027 como parte de unas reformas radicales del organismo rector del fútbol mundial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Federación de Fútbol de Países Bajos (KNVB) anunció que quiere organizar una cumbre internacional en Ámsterdam para reformar por completo la FIFA, al tiempo que pidió que el presidente Gianni Infantino sea sustituido antes de 2027 como parte de unas reformas radicales del organismo rector del fútbol mundial. La KNVB, uno de los miembros fundadores de la FIFA en 1904, dijo el domingo en un comunicado que ha perdido la confianza en Infantino y que desea reestructurar por completo la FIFA, en lugar de limitarse a cambiar a sus máximos dirigentes. Infantino se presentará a la reelección en marzo, pero las potencias regionales del fútbol mundial están debatiendo si presentar una moción de censura tras su fallida propuesta de vender una participación en eventos de la FIFA, como el Mundial, a inversores de capital privado. "La KNVB ya no tiene confianza en el liderazgo del presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino. Creemos que la FIFA necesita un nuevo liderazgo a partir de 2027", afirmó en un comunicado. "Pero un nuevo presidente por sí solo no basta. La forma en que se gobierna la FIFA también debe cambiar". "La KNVB apoyó a Infantino en las últimas elecciones presidenciales. Ese apoyo nunca fue incondicional", agregó. Asimismo, propuso celebrar una "Cumbre Internacional sobre el Futuro de la FIFA" en Ámsterdam, haciendo hincapié en que dicha cita debería determinar "qué tipo de FIFA queremos" antes de designar a un nuevo liderazgo. "Observamos que hay demasiado poder concentrado en torno al presidente de la FIFA y una separación insuficiente entre el presidente y la administración de la FIFA", añadieron. Reuters se ha puesto en contacto con la FIFA para recabar sus comentarios. El organismo neerlandés esbozó tres prioridades de reforma: una mejor gobernanza con controles y contrapesos más sólidos, situar los derechos humanos y la sostenibilidad en el centro de la toma de decisiones, y una cooperación internacional más estrecha. También quiere que la FIFA se esfuerce por reinvertir hasta el 90% de sus ingresos distribuibles en el desarrollo del fútbol. Infantino afirmó la semana pasada que era tarea de la FIFA reducir la brecha entre sus miembros más ricos y aquellos que cuentan con pocos recursos económicos. "Esto no debería ser un plan europeo para el resto del mundo", afirmó la KNVB. "Queremos desarrollar esta nueva orientación junto con las 211 federaciones miembro de la FIFA y las confederaciones de todas las partes del mundo". La KNVB forma parte de la UEFA, que solicitó a un tribunal federal estadounidense permiso para obtener testimonios y documentos de entidades de la FIFA en Florida con el fin de utilizarlos en una denuncia penal prevista en Suiza contra Infantino.

item.title: Gaza-Une frappe israélienne fait deux morts, dont un garçon de 3 ans - sources médicales
item.description: Une frappe aérienne israélienne a tué dimanche deux Palestiniens, dont un enfant de trois ans, dans le centre de la bande de Gaza, ont indiqué les autorités sanitaires de l'enclave.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une frappe aérienne israélienne a tué dimanche deux Palestiniens, dont un enfant de trois ans, dans le centre de la bande de Gaza, ont indiqué les autorités sanitaires de l'enclave. Selon elles, la frappe aérienne, survenue près d'une boulangerie à Deir Al Balah, a tué un homme, Hussam Nusair, et un garçon de trois ans, Tayyem Hamdan, et blessé plusieurs autres personnes. L'armée israélienne a déclaré avoir attaqué et tué un militant du Hamas. Elle a affirmé qu'Hussam Nusair avait mené des attaques contre les forces israéliennes et des civils. Le Hamas n'a pas fait dans l'immédiat de commentaires sur les allégations de l'armée israélienne. Un cessez-le-feu conclu en octobre 2025, sous l'égide des Etats-Unis, est censé avoir mis fin aux combats dans l'enclave palestinienne, mais Israël y poursuit ses frappes, affirmant vouloir contrecarrer les attaques du Hamas et d'autres groupes de militants. Le Hamas accuse Israël de violer le cessez-le-feu et de saper les efforts visant à mettre en œuvre un plan plus large du président américain Donald Trump pour mettre fin au conflit à Gaza, qui prévoit également le retrait israélien et le désarmement du Hamas. Plus de 1.300 Palestiniens ont été tués à Gaza depuis l'entrée en vigueur du cessez-le-feu en octobre dernier, selon le décompte des autorités sanitaires de Gaza, tandis que l'armée israélienne fait état de la mort de quatre de ses soldats.

item.title: Nepal steps up rescue effort to reach hundreds trapped in tunnels
item.description: Nepal's military airlifted heavy machinery by helicopter on Sunday to an under-construction dam high in the Himalayas as rescuers battled rising waters to reach workers in a tunnel, four days after catastrophic floods trapped them inside.
item.dc:creator: Sahana Bajracharya, Gopal Sharma
item.content:encoded: Nepal's military airlifted heavy machinery by helicopter on Sunday to an under-construction dam high in the Himalayas as rescuers battled rising waters to reach workers in a tunnel, four days after catastrophic floods trapped them inside. The torrent of ice, rock and debris that swept down a mountain valley on the China-Nepal border on Wednesday [USN:L4N44R005 TEXT:"killed more than 780 people"], left more than 3,000 missing, knocked out about 10% of Nepal's power generation capacity and inundated several hydropower projects under construction. Rescue operations are underway at five hydroelectric projects, including a major effort at the Upper Trishuli complex, where authorities said on Friday they received information that around 350 people could be trapped inside a tunnel. About 10,000 Nepali troops have been deployed for tunnel rescue operations alongside specialists from China and India, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of Nepal's national disaster management authority. "It's very tough because there's a lot of debris and we cannot blast things to make our way through," he said. A team of rescuers and soldiers worked through the night at Upper Trishuli, Nepali Prime Minister Balen Shah's office said on Sunday, posting video on social media showing a helicopter carrying heavy machinery to the area. "Rescue efforts continued despite the severe flooding last night," it said. The Upper Trishuli Hydropower 3A and 3B are interconnected hydropower plants on the Trishuli river, spanning Nepal's Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts, which were both hit hard by the floods. TEAMS REACH TUNNEL ENTRANCE China and India have each airlifted specialised tunnel rescue teams that are assisting Nepali authorities at the hydropower projects, according to their foreign ministries. Rescuers reached the entrance of one tunnel on Sunday and began clearing debris blocking access, officials said, marking the first breakthrough in the effort to reach those feared trapped inside. Once entry is secured, teams carrying oxygen supplies and cameras will move inside to assess conditions, search for survivors and provide the first images from within the tunnel, officials said. The Nepali army released a photograph showing two men caked in mud after being pulled from the mouth of one of the tunnels. An estimated 35 to 40 people could be trapped inside Tunnel 3A, where rescue personnel have widened the face of the passage after locating it on Sunday, said Nishesh Shrestha, aide to Nepali lawmaker Sagar Dhakal, who is at the site. "This figure is based on information gathered from people in nearby villages and has not been independently confirmed," Shrestha told Reuters. Officials estimate the main working area lies about 180 metres inside the tunnel. Reaching it could provide the first clear indication of the condition and location of any workers trapped underground.

item.title: Google Maps will show 'Lake America' in US, not 'Lake Ontario'
item.description: The president's order does not have any impact on Canadian naming conventions or how the rest of the world refers to the lake.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Google Maps has changed the name of "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" for U.S. users to reflect President Donald Trump's executive order renaming the lake, according to a Google statement. Trump announced on Thursday that he was [USN:S0N43F06A TEXT:"changing the name"] of the smallest of the five Great Lakes, part of an escalating trade feud with Canada that has prompted the two countries to impose reciprocal tariffs on billions of dollars in goods. The president's order affects the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), which sets the standards for official U.S. maps. It does not have any impact on Canadian naming conventions or how the rest of the world refers to the lake. "Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S., people using Maps in the U.S. will see 'Lake America,' those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario,' and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names," Google said in a blog post issued on Saturday. The White House, Carney's office and Ford's office did not immediately comment on Sunday on Google's decision. Google Maps made a similar change to the Gulf of Mexico last year, labeling it the "Gulf of America" following Trump's executive order on his first day in office renaming the body of water. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney immediately rejected the lake's name change on Thursday. Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul of New York, which shares a long border with Canada, declared that "New York won't be calling it that," while Phil Scott, the Republican governor of neighboring Vermont, called Trump's decision "petty and disappointing" on social media. The premier of Ontario, Doug Ford, on Saturday unveiled a large lakeside sign that reads, "Lake Ontario: Now and Always," in both English and French. "President Trump can call it whatever he wants, but I can tell you, the rest of the world will always call it Lake Ontario," Ford said.

item.title: Alcaraz, Sabalenka launch bids to retain US Open crowns
item.description: The return of Carlos Alcaraz to competitive tennis has been one of the biggest talking points at the U.S. Open as he partnered with Serena Williams in the mixed doubles and reached the quarter-finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Both defending champions enter the fray as the U.S. Open's first round continues on Monday, with Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz looking for their third titles. TOP MEN'S MATCH: ROMAN SAFIULLIN V CARLOS ALCARAZ World number three Alcaraz won three of the last four Grand Slams before a wrist injury forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon. The Spaniard's return to competitive tennis has been one of the biggest talking points at the U.S. Open, as he partnered with Serena Williams in the mixed doubles and reached the quarter-finals. "You're going to see Carlitos playing the way he always has... I need competition. It wasn't an easy decision. I just did whatever it took to be ready," the 23-year-old said. Alcaraz faces a tricky opponent. Safiullin beat him in 2023, the only time they have met on a hard court. Alcaraz beat the Russian at the Paris Olympics the following year, on clay. "I'm not going to set a limit for myself. I don't want to focus on a specific result. I want to focus on the process we've gone through. Just go out there, enjoy it and feel good," Alcaraz added. TOP WOMEN'S MATCH: ARYNA SABALENKA V CAMILA OSORIO After two semi-final runs and defeat in the 2023 final, Sabalenka captured the U.S. Open crown in 2024 and repeated the feat the following year. The world number one now has the opportunity to become the 12th woman to win the title three times in a row, the first since Serena Williams did it between 2012 and 2014. But although the four-times Grand Slam winner continues to dominate the rankings, the 27-year-old's form has hit a slump. She has not reached a WTA tournament final since March, and suffered round-of-16 exits at the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open this month. "It wasn't the best period... I've been dealing with several things. But who cares, right? Yeah, I didn't perform my best," Sabalenka told reporters. OSAKA LOOKS TO EXCEL IN 'SIDE HUSTLE' Four-times Grand Slam winner Osaka reached the U.S. Open semi-finals last year, and followed that up with last month's quarter-final run at Wimbledon. "I think people forget my main job is to be a mom. This is kind of like my side hustle a little bit. I just happen to be really good at it," Osaka said. "I feel good. I'm coming off of... Toronto, and that was a pretty good result for me. So, yeah, I guess we'll see what happens," she added. U.S. OPEN ORDER OF PLAY ON MONDAY (prefix number denotes seeding): ARTHUR ASHE STADIUM (1530 GMT/1130 ET) 1-Aryna Sabalenka (Belarus) v Camila Osorio (Colombia) Roman Safiullin (Russia) v 2-Carlos Alcaraz (Spain) 8-Ben Shelton (U.S.) v Tallon Griekspoor (Netherlands) 13-Naomi Osaka (Japan) v Anastasia Zakharova (Russia) LOUIS ARMSTRONG STADIUM (1500 GMT/1100 ET) Stefanos Tsitsipas (Greece) v 10-Arthur Fils (France) Ashlyn Krueger (U.S.) v 10-Amanda Anisimova (U.S.) 8-Iga Swiatek (Poland) v Wang Xiyu (China) Martin Damm (U.S.) v 11-Frances Tiafoe (U.S.)

item.title: Julián Álvarez vuelve a entrenamientos del Atlético mientras siguen especulaciones sobre el Barcelona
item.description: Julián Álvarez volvió a los entrenamientos del Atlético de Madrid el domingo, en medio de los continuos rumores sobre el interés del Fútbol Club Barcelona por el delantero argentino.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Julián Álvarez volvió a los entrenamientos del Atlético de Madrid el domingo, en medio de los continuos rumores sobre el interés del Fútbol Club Barcelona por el delantero argentino. Álvarez se perdió las tres sesiones de entrenamiento del equipo rojiblanco a finales de la semana pasada debido a lo que el club describió como una "indisposición", antes de entrenar en solitario el viernes por la tarde. No fue convocado para la victoria por 3-1 del sábado en Sevilla, un resultado que desvió brevemente la atención hacia el terreno de juego. "El plan es clarísimo. Julián tuvo unos días que no se encontró bien. Ayer ya se entrenó y esperamos que se reintegre rápidamente y que esté disponible espero el próximo partido de LaLiga. Hablamos mucho con él todos", dijo a la prensa Mateu Alemany, director de fútbol profesional del Atlético, antes del partido contra el Sevilla. El mercado de fichajes de LaLiga se cierra el martes y la situación sigue siendo tensa. El consejero delegado del Atlético, Miguel Ángel Gil Marín, acusó al Barcelona de falta de honestidad la semana pasada y afirmó que Álvarez nunca sería vendido al club catalán. Según fuentes cercanas a la situación, el Arsenal es la única alternativa viable en caso de que el club de la Premier League presente una oferta de alrededor de 150 millones de euros (174 millones de dólares). Álvarez declaró durante el Mundial que "quería cumplir su sueño" de jugar en el Barcelona. (1 dólar = 0,8634 euros)

item.title: Níger dice que recuperó el control de una base aérea tras un motín de soldados
item.description: Níger afirmó que había recuperado el control de una base aérea militar clave en la capital, Niamey, tras un ataque perpetrado el sábado por soldados amotinados, en lo que supone el último desafío al gobernante militar Abdourahamane Tiani, mientras su Gobierno lucha por contener una insurgencia yihadista.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Níger afirmó que había recuperado el control de una base aérea militar clave en la capital, Niamey, tras un ataque perpetrado el sábado por soldados amotinados, en lo que supone el último desafío al gobernante militar Abdourahamane Tiani, mientras su Gobierno lucha por contener una insurgencia yihadista. El ataque puso de manifiesto las tensiones existentes en el seno de las fuerzas armadas de Níger, que han sufrido repetidas derrotas en el campo de batalla mientras luchan contra los grupos afiliados a Al Qaeda y Estado Islámico en África Occidental. El sábado por la mañana se escucharon explosiones y disparos en toda Niamey, incluso en la base aérea militar y en los alrededores de la presidencia. Situada en el mismo complejo que el aeropuerto civil de Niamey, la base aérea alberga aviones militares y drones, así como una unidad antiterrorista de la Alianza de Estados del Sahel (AES), de la que forman parte Níger, Malí y Burkina Faso. También hay fuerzas rusas e italianas estacionadas allí. El Cuerpo de África, una fuerza paramilitar controlada por el Kremlin, recibió una solicitud de ayuda para neutralizar a los amotinados en Niamey, según declaró el sábado Viktor Voropaev, embajador ruso en Níger, en una entrevista con la agencia de noticias TASS. Antes del ataque del sábado, la base aérea ya había sido objeto de dos asaltos este año: en enero, por parte de la filial regional de Estado Islámico, y en junio, de su par de Al Qaeda. Los medios estatales informaron a última hora del sábado de que en el ataque participaron "cientos de soldados descontentos" y que los combates se prolongaron durante varias horas mientras las fuerzas leales al líder militar Tiani intentaban recuperar el control. Se emitieron imágenes que, supuestamente, mostraban a los amotinados rindiéndose. Reuters no pudo confirmar de forma independiente la información de los medios estatales. La Guardia Presidencial acudió en defensa de Tiani, según indicaron tres fuentes de seguridad. Tiani no había hecho ninguna aparición pública hasta la mañana del domingo. Níger, un país de África Occidental rico en recursos de uranio, petróleo y oro, ha estado gobernado por militares desde el golpe de Estado de julio de 2023 que derrocó al presidente Mohamed Bazoum. LUCHA CONTRA LOS YIHADISTAS Tiani, al igual que sus homólogos de Burkina Faso y Malí, no ha logrado avances contra los yihadistas. La filial de Estado Islámico ha perpetrado múltiples ataques mortales contra el ejército en el suroeste de Níger, incluido uno a principios de este mes en el que murieron 18 soldados. En la operación de los amotinados participaron soldados destinados en Niamey, así como soldados de las localidades de Ouallam, Tera y Dosso, donde el ejército ha sufrido numerosas bajas. Analistas y fuentes de seguridad afirman que la frustración con el Gobierno va en aumento entre las unidades de primera línea, lo que supone otra vulnerabilidad para Tiani más allá de los propios insurgentes. Desde que tomó el poder, el Gobierno de Tiani se ha alejado de sus socios occidentales, ha estrechado los lazos con Rusia y ha roto con el bloque regional de la CEDEAO. Los disturbios se producen en un momento en que las autoridades endurecen el control sobre el sector del uranio, tras haber confiscado activos de la empresa francesa Orano. Níger era un proveedor clave de combustible nuclear para Europa, representando cerca del 15% del suministro de uranio de Orano a pleno rendimiento.

item.title: Ukraine defence chief pledges 'clear' war plan to win early loan release
item.description: Ukraine's new defence minister pledged a "clear" vision for Kyiv's partners on how his country plans to fight Russia with more resources, in a bid to bring forward part of a European Union loan to help cover a $27 billion military budget deficit.
item.dc:creator: Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Ukraine's new defence minister pledged a "clear" vision for Kyiv's partners on how his country plans to fight Russia with more resources, in a bid to bring forward part of a European Union loan to help cover a $27 billion military budget deficit. The Ukrainian government relies heavily on foreign funds to continue its war effort, now in its fifth year, with [USN:L1N425047 TEXT:"the EU committing"] €90 billion in financing through 2027. In comments to reporters released on Sunday, Yevhenii Khmara said Kyiv would seek to bring forward part of the €45 billion loan planned for next year, as well as lobby allies for greater contributions and new countries that had not yet given. "Ukraine will present partners with a clear vision and a clear plan: what tasks the Defence Forces face, what projects are needed for this, what results must be achieved, and within what timeframes," he said. The EU has earmarked €45 billion each for 2026 and 2027, allowing Ukraine to channel record funds toward defence. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:L1N44K01P TEXT:"said last week"] that Kyiv had spent more than expected in the first half of the year. 'COMMON VISION' FOR WAR Khmara took over as defence minister last month from Mykhailo Fedorov, whose dismissal sparked rare wartime protests that prompted Zelenskiy to also fire his unpopular military chief. A former special-forces commander credited with leading Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against Russia, Khmara said he shared a "common vision" with new top general Mykhailo Drapatyi. Kyiv is seeking to [USN:L1N44N0HZ TEXT:"seize the initiative"] from Moscow, partly by stepping up long-range drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, defence manufacturing and logistics. But it faces a critical shortage of manpower and air defences to fend off Russian air attacks on Ukrainian cities. Kyiv's military has also faced controversy over abuses and mismanagement in recruitment and on the battlefield. Khmara said Ukraine needs "proper decisions" to preserve lives and a clear vision throughout the ranks for how to fight and end the war. "This vision must be communicated down the chain to commanders and units carrying out missions at the front every day," he said. Khmara said Ukraine has tested four potential interceptors to shoot down the jet-powered drones Russia is increasingly firing at Ukraine. Swarms of the high-speed drones have [USN:L1N44Q02Y TEXT:"plagued the capital Kyiv"] for four consecutive days, killing residents, damaging homes and warehouses and upending daily life.

item.title: Astros playing for AL West title; Mets' Juan Soto looking ahead to future
item.description: Juan Soto didn't want to wait any longer to get in on the fun with the suddenly resurgent New York Mets.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Juan Soto didn't want to wait any longer to get in on the fun with the suddenly resurgent New York Mets. Soto and the Mets will look to earn their fifth series win over a contender this month on Sunday afternoon when they host the Houston Astros in the finale of a three-game interleague set. Left-hander Zac Thornton (3-4, 2.88 ERA) is slated to pitch for the Mets against Astros right-hander Ethan Pecko (0-0, 7.88), who will make his third big league start. Soto returned from the injured list and hit the tie-breaking RBI single in the fifth inning Saturday as the Mets beat the Astros 6-2. Soto sat out the previous five weeks due to a strained left calf and watched as the Mets won 17 of 31 games without him -- even though president of baseball operations David Stearns worked to dismantle one of the league's most disappointing teams by dealing seven veterans at the Aug. 3 trade deadline. The only tangible goal left this season for New York is to avoid finishing last in the National League East for the first time since 2003. The Mets are three games behind the fourth-place Washington Nationals. But Soto is hoping the final five weeks can provide a foundation for a return to contention for the Mets. New York's core next season likely will consist of Francisco Lindor, another veteran hoping to bounce back from an injury-riddled season, as well as rookie outfielders Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing and young starting pitchers Thornton, Nolan McLean and Christian Scott. McLean earned the win Saturday, when he allowed two hits and an unearned run over seven innings. He has lasted at least six innings in 13 of his past 15 starts. All but two were quality starts. "Seeing how everything is clicking for us, I think it's really cool to see -- it means a lot, not only for this year, but for the next years coming," Soto said. "I'm just really happy about it, the way we've been playing. And that's another thing too that motivated me a little bit more to come back, to try to join this positive wave." For the Astros, the struggles of opener Bennett Sousa and bulk reliever Cristian Javier on Saturday offered another reminder why Houston lured former pitching coach Brent Strom out of retirement this week to serve as a consultant to current pitching coaches Josh Miller and Ethan Katz. Sousa, making his first big league start in 99 games, gave up a run while getting just two outs before giving way to Javier, who didn't allow a run until the Mets' go-ahead rally in the fifth. He gave up three runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings. The only Astros pitchers with at least eight starts and an ERA below 4.00 are Hunter Brown and Peter Lambert. Brown, who was Houston's Opening Day starter but missed 2 1/2 months with a right shoulder injury, pitched 6 2/3 innings in a 3-1 win on Friday -- the longest start for the club since Hayden Wesneski went seven innings on Aug. 10. Despite the pitching woes, the Astros are two games ahead of the Texas Rangers in the American League West. Strom told reporters on Saturday that he is there to provide "just a different set of eyes and ears." "It's exciting to join a first-place team," he said. Neither Thornton nor Pecko factored into the decision in their most recent starts Tuesday night. Thornton allowed one run over six innings in the Mets' 3-2, 10-inning win over the Milwaukee Brewers. Across town, Pecko gave up five runs over 4 1/3 innings as the Astros beat the host New York Yankees, 9-7. Thornton has never faced the Astros and Pecko has never opposed the Mets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong, host Cubs seek to shine in prime time vs. Reds
item.description: Chicago Cubs slugger Pete Crow-Armstrong will look to continue to bolster his resume for the 2026 National League MVP award on Sunday night when he takes center stage in a nationally televised game against the visiting Cincinnati Reds.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Chicago Cubs slugger Pete Crow-Armstrong will look to continue to bolster his resume for the 2026 National League MVP award on Sunday night when he takes center stage in a nationally televised game against the visiting Cincinnati Reds. Crow-Armstrong recorded his first career three-homer performance and drove in six runs during Chicago's 17-5 romp over Cincinnati on Saturday. The victory snapped a three-game skid for the Cubs and evened the three-game series against the Reds at one victory apiece. Crow-Armstrong raised his team-leading homer total to 36 on the season with a solo shot in the first inning, a two-run blast in the second and a three-run homer in the seventh. And he did so shortly after news circulated that four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers continued to feel discomfort in his left knee coming off his latest bullpen session. Fans at Wrigley Field weren't shy about sharing their unofficial votes for the award, serenading Crow-Armstrong with chants of "M-V-P! M-V-P!" Crow-Armstrong told Marquee Sports Network that he was told by a Cubs legend that he was going to enjoy a power surge on Saturday. "Sammy Sosa told me I was gonna hit 3 and I hit 3. Put that on the record," Crow-Armstrong said. Said Cubs manager Craig Counsell: "I think Pete's having a wonderful season. It's a lot of fun to watch ... Pete's done a couple things this year that haven't been done in a long time." Carson Kelly added a three-run homer, Seiya Suzuki had a two-run shot and Alex Bregman also went deep to highlight the Cubs' 19-hit attack. Cincinnati right-hander Chase Burns (14-3, 2.77 ERA) will look to keep Crow-Armstrong and company in check on Sunday night. Burns allowed five runs for the second time in four outings on Monday, this time in 3 2/3 innings in a 5-0 loss to the San Francisco Giants. He shared the plan for him going forward as he heads into the final month of the season. "This season, making every start and limiting my pitch count and innings, that's huge for my body," Burns said, per Charlie Goldsmith of Charlie's Chalkboard. "That's the plan. Making every start is the biggest thing. I don't need to go out there at the end of September and throw 110 pitches. Make every start if I feel great. Constantly communicate with them." Burns, 23, will make his first career start versus the Cubs after working 1 1/3 innings in relief against them on Sept. 20 of last season. He allowed one run on three hits in that game. Chicago left-hander Shota Imanaga (8-9, 3.78) will get the start on Sunday. Imanaga received his third straight no-decision last Sunday after permitting two runs (one earned) on five hits in two innings against the Seattle Mariners. He threw 72 pitches in the short outing. He split a pair of decisions versus Cincinnati this season despite yielding just one run in each contest. Imanaga is 2-1 with a 2.48 ERA in five career appearances (all starts) against the Reds. The third-year MLB pro will need to tread carefully around rookie Sal Stewart, who has gone deep in both games of this series and three times over his last four contests overall. --Field Level Media

item.title: Phillies' Zack Wheeler strives to get back on track vs. Angels
item.description: Coming off his worst start of the season, right-hander Zack Wheeler will try and help pitch the Philadelphia Phillies to a sweep of their three-game series versus the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday afternoon in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Coming off his worst start of the season, right-hander Zack Wheeler will try and help pitch the Philadelphia Phillies to a sweep of their three-game series versus the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday afternoon in Anaheim, Calif. Wheeler (10-5, 3.40 ERA) has struggled badly since allowing two hits and striking out 10 over six innings in his last start before the All-Star break. He was 10-1 with a 2.13 ERA and in the thick of the National League Cy Young race following that win. The worm has turned for Wheeler, who fell to 0-4 since that start after allowing a season-high eight earned runs on nine hits -- including four home runs -- and five walks in four-plus innings in a 9-2 loss to the Seattle Mariners. Wheeler claims he's feeling fine despite the drastic downturn. "I'm healthy, strong -- everything's there," said Wheeler, who missed the end of the 2025 season with venous thoracic outlet syndrome and a right shoulder blood clot. "So, I just don't know. Just got to zone it back in and figure it out. "I'm just really struggling the past few. All I can really throw for a strike - a good quality strike - is a fastball right now, and that's not even fully consistent. So when you're pitching kind of with one pitch, it's pretty hard up here." The good news is that Wheeler will be facing an Angels team that has lost six straight and is in a dead heat with the Colorado Rockies for the worst record in baseball. Wheeler is 3-0 with a 2.81 ERA in three career appearances (all starts) against Los Angeles. Left-hander Yusei Kikuchi (0-4, 6.25) will make his second start since coming off the 60-day injured list after missing four months with left shoulder inflammation. It will be his first start at Angel Stadium since April 18 when he allowed four hits and one earned run over six innings while striking out eight in a 4-1 loss to the San Diego Padres. Kikuchi gave up five runs on seven hits in five innings in his return from the injured list on Sunday, a 5-3 loss to the Texas Rangers. The good news was that his fastball averaged 96 mph, a slight increase from where it was when he went on the injured list. "I thought the stuff was good," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki told the Orange County Register. "The velo was up. It just came down to execution, with two strikes. He did a really good job of getting to two strikes, and then with two strikes, the execution wasn't as good, and those are the mistakes they hit." Kikuchi is 0-0 with a 2.45 ERA in two career starts against Philadelphia. The Angels have lost all six games during their losing streak by two runs or fewer, including 4-2 in 10 innings on Saturday. Twice they lost despite leading going into the ninth inning, including Friday's series opener when Edmundo Sosa hit a two-out, pinch-hit grand slam to give the Phillies a 5-3 victory. "It's definitely heartbreaking, gut-wrenching, whatever you want to call it," Suzuki said. "But at the same time, they're professionals and, like I've said, these guys are resilient, man. ... They'll never stop fighting. They'll never stop battling." --Field Level Media

item.title: Policía busca al autor de un tiroteo mortal en una fiesta rave en Suiza
item.description: Una mujer de 22 años murió y otras cinco personas resultaron heridas, algunas de gravedad, en un tiroteo ocurrido en una fiesta rave en la localidad suiza de Aarau, según informó este domingo la policía local.
item.dc:creator: Romina Amato
item.content:encoded: Una mujer de 22 años murió y otras cinco personas resultaron heridas, algunas de gravedad, en un tiroteo ocurrido en una fiesta rave en la localidad suiza de Aarau, según informó este domingo la policía local. Todas las víctimas son residentes en Suiza y tienen entre 20 y 30 años, según la policía, que añadió que se está buscando a los responsables y se habían acordonado amplias zonas de la ciudad. La policía pidió a la ciudadanía que facilite cualquier imagen del incidente. Un testigo de 34 años que pidió permanecer en el anonimato declaró a Reuters que oyó disparos poco después de que la música se detuviera a las 2:30 de la madrugada del domingo, lo que en un primer momento confundió con fuegos artificiales. Algunos se refugiaron detrás de la cabina del DJ y una mujer se escondió detrás de una nevera, pero recibió un disparo en la espalda y se desangró hasta morir a pesar de los esfuerzos por reanimarla, explicó. "Es increíblemente trágico. Era joven", dijo a Reuters. "Que algo así pueda ocurrir en Aarau, en un evento local, es sencillamente inimaginable. Todavía no me lo puedo creer". La policía informó de que una mujer de 22 años falleció a causa de sus heridas en el lugar de los hechos. Los agentes reforzaron su presencia más allá de la localidad —situada a unos 50 kilómetros al oeste de Zúrich— como medida de precaución. Imágenes de Reuters mostraron a agentes armados patrullando la zona, convoyes policiales circulando por las calles y vehículos blindados aparcados cerca del lugar de los hechos. La página web de los organizadores anunciaba el evento como una fiesta techno en un hipódromo cubierto, a la que se esperaba que asistieran 3.500 personas. Suiza tiene una de las tasas más altas de posesión de armas de Europa, aunque los tiroteos son poco frecuentes y en 2019 aprobó normas más estrictas de control de armas.

item.title: Chelsea ficha al arquero argentino "Dibu" Martínez procedente del Villa, con contrato de tres años
item.description: El Chelsea anunció el domingo el fichaje del arquero argentino Emiliano "Dibu" Martínez, procedente del Aston Villa, con un contrato de tres años.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Chelsea anunció el domingo el fichaje del arquero argentino Emiliano "Dibu" Martínez, procedente del Aston Villa, con un contrato de tres años. No se revelaron los detalles económicos, pero los medios británicos informaron de que el club del oeste de Londres pagó unos 7,5 millones de libras esterlinas (10,15 millones de dólares) para fichar al jugador de 33 años. "Quiero triunfar aquí", declaró Martínez en un comunicado. "Soy una persona que quiere ganar en todo lo que hago y quiero aportar eso a este club de fútbol, porque es un club que gana títulos, así que creo que es una buena combinación". La salida del "Dibu" se produce después de que el Villa fichara este mes al internacional japonés Zion Suzuki, procedente del Parma, lo que allanó el camino para la salida del argentino tras seis años en Villa Park. Disputó 256 partidos con el Villa tras llegar procedente del Arsenal en 2020 y se consolidó como uno de los arqueros más destacados de la Premier League. Desempeñó un papel clave la temporada pasada, cuando el equipo de Unai Emery terminó cuarto, clasificándose para la Liga de Campeones, y ganó la Liga Europa. En el Chelsea competirá con Robert Sánchez por la titularidad. Sánchez ha sido el portero titular del Chelsea desde que llegó procedente del Brighton & Hove Albion en 2023, pero las dudas sobre su puesto resurgieron tras los errores cometidos en la victoria por 3-2 del Chelsea sobre el Fulham en la jornada inaugural. Martínez también ha sido fundamental para el éxito de Argentina en la escena internacional, ayudando a su selección a ganar el Mundial de 2022 y ser subcampeona en 2026. También se alzó con los títulos de la Copa América en 2021 y 2024. (1 dólar = 0,7390 libras)

item.title: Pirates strive for better defensive play in finale vs. Cards
item.description: With the Major League Baseball postseason an unlikely destination again for the Pittsburgh Pirates, they probably will focus on the process more than results the rest of the way.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: With the Major League Baseball postseason an unlikely destination again for the Pittsburgh Pirates, they probably will focus on the process more than results the rest of the way. While pleased with some details in a 6-2 victory against the host St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday, Pittsburgh manager Don Kelly conceded his team was lucky to escape after making multiple defensive miscues. If the Pirates want to win the series finale Sunday afternoon and what comes after, they will need to clean up their fielding. "We gave them way too many outs," Kelly said. "You can't win many baseball games playing like that." Rookie slugger Rafael Flores Jr. belted a three-run homer, Brandon Lowe added a solo shot and the Pittsburgh bullpen allowed one run and two hits over 6 2/3 innings. But it wasn't all good news. The Pirates made errors on three consecutive plays that led to a Cardinals run in the bottom of the sixth inning, but right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski limited the damage and pitched out of a jam. "Carmen just flat-lined all the way through it," Kelly said, referring to the pitcher staying calm despite the trouble. Three innings earlier, Mlodzinski had come in with the bases loaded and two outs when slugger Jordan Walker flied out to center. Flores, who was catching, took note of Mlodzinski's total effort with the team jammed up. "I mean, cold-blooded," Flores said. "In those situations you want the guy with the lowest heartbeat, and that was Carmen Mlodzinski. He made sure he kept breathing, made sure he kept executing, and he got out of it." As for the defensive lapses, which included two botched grounders by shortstop Jacob Gonzalez and a whiff by outfielder Oneil Cruz on a routine fly to center, Kelly said team meetings would not be forthcoming. "They know they need to make the plays," Kelly said. "It's something that just snowballed right there. Everybody who's played the game knows how fast it goes, so when it starts snowballing, you have to learn how to slow it down." Kelly noted that the Pirates also made three errors in a losing effort on Friday night. "We need to slow down and make the plays," Kelly said. Right-hander Braxton Ashcraft (13-5, 3.59 ERA) will get the start in the finale after producing resurgent performances in five outings this month. He owns a 1.91 ERA with 26 strikeouts, four walks and just 17 hits allowed in his past 33 innings. Ashcraft's results against the Cardinals this season have been mixed; he allowed six runs and two homers in a loss in late April, and just one run with nine strikeouts over seven innings in a win three weeks later. Ashcraft is 1-1 with a 4.24 ERA in three career appearances (all starts) versus St. Louis. The Cardinals counter with left-hander Matthew Liberatore (5-12, 5.44), who owns a 7.97 ERA in his past four starts. He also allowed four runs and struck out nine in 4 2/3 innings against the Pirates in May. Liberatore is 2-3 with a 5.72 ERA in 11 career appearances (seven starts) versus Pittsburgh. The Cards likely hope for a longer outing from Liberatore after using right-hander Kyle Leahy for a short stint Saturday. He went three innings as the team regulates his workload. Leahy has logged 129 1/3 innings this season after performing as a short reliever previously. "He's capped," Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said of Leahy. "I'd love to see him go longer but that's not the plan." The Pirates announced that rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin would start a minor-league injury rehab assignment with Double-A Altoona on Sunday. He is eligible to come off the 60-day injured list Friday after being out since early July because of a torn ligament on his left ring finger. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jackson Chourio, Brewers aim for sweep of Rangers
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy is running out of superlatives to describe left fielder Jackson Chourio, who has entered the record books in just his third season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy is running out of superlatives to describe left fielder Jackson Chourio, who has entered the record books in just his third season. Chourio has homered three times in Milwaukee's last three contests. The Brewers look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Texas Rangers on Sunday. Chourio and William Contreras each homered in the first inning in the Brewers' 5-3 win on Saturday. Chourio's blast was his 20th homer of the season. The 22-year old has recorded three consecutive 20-homer seasons to begin his career, and he is the 17th player in major league history with at least three seasons of 20 or more home runs by his age-22 season. "And he's still learning the game," Murphy said. "Man, he's special. His hands go from A to B as quick as anybody. Bat speed and strength, he's got a great base underneath him. And the great thing is, he comes every day with a smile on his face. He doesn't get too down ... He's special." Milwaukee won its fourth straight game on Saturday despite an off night at the plate by leadoff hitter Brice Turang, who went 0-for-4 with three strikeouts. "Brice has been doing it for three years now," Murphy said. "He can do it. He's banged up, he's lost weight. His offense tonight was not what he wanted, but he still goes out and plays defense. That's the mental toughness the guy has." Texas has lost four straight and sits two games behind the American League West-leading Houston Astros and two games behind Cleveland in the chase for the AL's final wild card spot. Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said his team is still searching for its identity on offense. "Finding different ways to beat a team is kind of what I want it to be," Schumaker said. "Trying to create that over the next 20-plus games is what we are going to have to figure out." One component of Schumaker's plan is to have speedy outfielder Evan Carter increase his number of bunt hits. He has just five this season. "I'd love to be that kind of player where you lead off and, on the first pitch of the game, you lay down a bunt and - oh, my gosh - you can feel it right away," Carter said. "I bunt a lot, probably work on it half the days of the week. I'm trying to work on it as much as I can." Texas will send right-hander Kumar Rocker (5-10, 4.41 ERA) to the mound in the series finale. He yielded two runs in 5 2/3 innings in an 11-2 road win over the Chicago White Sox last Monday. Rocker, 26, is making his first career appearance against Milwaukee. The Brewers will counter with right-hander Dustin May (6-8, 4.56 ERA), who exited last Wednesday's start against the New York Mets after he was drilled in the shoulder by a line drive off the bat of A.J. Ewing on the first pitch of the game. May, 28, was able to play catch on Thursday and is set to make his fifth start with Milwaukee since being acquired from the St. Louis Cardinals on Aug. 3. Brandon Nimmo is 2-for-9 with six strikeouts against May, who owns a 3.86 ERA in two career starts versus Texas. -Field Level Media

item.title: Gulf stocks fall as Fed rate-hike bets rise after Warsh remarks
item.description: Most Gulf stock markets closed lower on Sunday as investors turned cautious after U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's commitment to bringing inflation back to target, boosting expectations of another interest-rate increase.
item.dc:creator: Md Hussain
item.content:encoded: Most Gulf stock markets closed lower on Sunday as investors turned cautious after U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's commitment to bringing inflation back to target, boosting expectations of another interest-rate increase. Warsh said at the Fed's annual economic symposium in Jackson Hole that policymakers would [USN:L6N44P0MM TEXT:""have work to do""] if they were not confident that underlying inflation was returning to the central bank's 2% target. He also noted that financial conditions did not appear restrictive. Following his remarks, market-implied [USN:L6N44P11M TEXT:"odds of a rate increase"] at the Fed's September meeting rose to 55.7% from 35.4% on Thursday, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. Gulf markets are particularly sensitive to changes in U.S. monetary-policy expectations since most regional currencies are pegged to the dollar. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) fell 0.7% for a second consecutive session, with most constituents ending in negative territory. Saudi Arabian Mining (1211.SE) declined 3.3%, while Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) , the kingdom's largest lender by assets, lost 1.2%. "The Saudi market could remain vulnerable to further downside if investors continue taking profits after several sessions of gains," said Hani Abuagla, senior market analyst at XTB MENA. Qatar's benchmark index (.QSI) edged 0.1% lower, weighed down by declines in financial and communications shares. Doha Bank (DOBK.QA) dropped 5.1%, while The Commercial Bank (COMB.QA) fell 2.5%. In contrast, QatarEnergy-linked Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA) gained 0.6%, and Gulf International Services (GISS.QA) rose 3.9%. QatarEnergy [USN:L1N44P049 TEXT:"sold at least 7 million barrels"] of various Qatari crude grades through a tender this week for October loading, several trade sources said on Friday. "Looking ahead, GCC markets are likely to remain sensitive to shipping developments in the Strait of Hormuz and any diplomatic progress," Abuagla said. "Strong domestic fundamentals may help limit downside risks, though investor caution could persist as global bond yields rose following Warsh's remarks, with attention now turning to the Fed's next meeting." Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) slipped 0.3%, with most shares trading lower. Commercial International Bank (COMI.CA) fell 0.8%, while Talaat Moustafa Group (TMGH.CA) lost 1.3%. Abu Qir Fertilizers and Chemical Industries (ABUK.CA) , however, rose 4.8% after the company said it had [USN:FWN44P1X6 TEXT:"expanded ammonia production"] capacity and reduced natural-gas consumption. SAUDI ARABIA (.TASI) down 0.7% to 11,159 QATAR (.QSI) fell 0.1% to 9,863 KUWAIT (.BKP) ended flat at 9,307 BAHRAIN (.BAX) fell 0.1% to 1,940 OMAN (.MSX30) up 0.6% to 7,578 EGYPT (.EGX30) lost 0.3% to 54,937

item.title: Islandia rechaza las negociaciones de adhesión a la UE en un reñido referéndum
item.description: Los islandeses votaron a favor de quedarse fuera de la Unión Europea, según revelaron el domingo los resultados del referéndum, al rechazar la iniciativa del Gobierno de reabrir las negociaciones de adhesión y dar la razón a quienes afirmaban que las aguas pesqueras de Islandia son demasiado importantes como para arriesgarlas.
item.dc:creator: Johan Ahlander, Tom Little
item.content:encoded: Los islandeses votaron a favor de quedarse fuera de la Unión Europea, según revelaron el domingo los resultados del referéndum, al rechazar la iniciativa del Gobierno de reabrir las negociaciones de adhesión y dar la razón a quienes afirmaban que las aguas pesqueras de Islandia son demasiado importantes como para arriesgarlas. Esta isla ártica de 400.000 habitantes lleva más de una década debatiendo si adherirse a la UE y, en un principio, se esperaba que respaldara por un estrecho margen la celebración de negociaciones de adhesión, aunque los sondeos de este mes revelaron que las opiniones habían cambiado. "Se trata de un claro revés para Bruselas", declaró a Reuters un diplomático de la UE, quien añadió que las cuestiones de la pesca y la independencia habían sido decisivas. En el referéndum del sábado, el 52,8% de los votos emitidos se opuso a la propuesta del Gobierno de entablar negociaciones con Bruselas y el 47,2% la respaldó, con una participación del 82,5% del electorado, según informaron la cadena pública RUV y otros medios locales. De las seis circunscripciones, solo las dos del centro de Reikiavik registraron una mayoría a favor, mientras que las zonas rurales y los suburbios capitalinos votaron en contra. El Gobierno presentó la adhesión como un escudo contra las guerras comerciales y la rivalidad en el Ártico, y planteó el referéndum como un momento de "ahora o nunca". La primera ministra, Kristrun Frostadottir, afirmó que un "no" pondría fin al debate mientras su coalición de centroizquierda estuviera en el poder. En Bruselas, algunos responsables habían expresado su esperanza de que un voto a favor de la adhesión por parte de Islandia pudiera mitigar el escepticismo hacia la ampliación de la UE y reforzar estratégicamente al bloque en un momento en que la seguridad en el Ártico ocupa un lugar central. Islandia, Estado miembro de la OTAN pero sin ejército propio, también debatió si la adhesión a la UE podría reforzar la seguridad del país, en un momento en que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha puesto en duda el compromiso de su país con la alianza militar. Trump también ha afirmado en repetidas ocasiones que quiere adquirir Groenlandia, otra isla del Ártico. Sin embargo, para algunos islandeses, la pesca era una cuestión más importante que la seguridad. Este sector es uno de los más importantes de Islandia, ya que representa el 15% del Producto Interno Bruto en contribuciones directas e indirectas, y alrededor del 40% de los ingresos por exportaciones, según muestran los datos.

item.title: Trump says NBC's Welker to be reported to FCC over characterization of his endorsement record
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post on Sunday that NBC's Kristen Welker will be reported to the Federal Communications Commission for "rebuke or punishment," after he said she reported the Republican president had mixed results in his endorsement of candidates.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post on Sunday that NBC's Kristen Welker will be reported to the Federal Communications Commission for "rebuke or punishment," after he said she reported the Republican president had mixed results in his endorsement of candidates. "Kristen Welker, the Unpopular 'Hostess' of the once great Meet the Press, now considered Meet the Fake Press, just stated that Donald Trump has 'mixed results' on his Endorsements of Candidates, when the recent WINS of Darline Graham and Mike Mazzei, stand at 100% for the U.S. Senate, and 98% for the U.S. House," Trump wrote. "Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment. Unfortunately, she is not the only one," Trump added in the post. NBC did not immediately respond to a question for comment. Trump's comments are the latest in an aggressive series of attacks he has leveled on the news media. He has repeatedly urged broadcasters to drop comedy or news programs he dislikes or which have been critical of him or his administration. ABC and its parent company Disney (DIS.N) [USN:L1N44F0BK TEXT:"sued the FCC"] earlier this month to block an early review of licenses for eight ABC stations, arguing that the Trump administration is trying to punish the network over its broadcast content. Trump has pressed the FCC on numerous occasions to revoke ABC's licenses. The FCC is also [USN:L1N3TR0R4 TEXT:"investigating"] NBC-parent Comcast's (CMCSA.O) relationships with its local broadcast TV affiliates, the latest in a series of probes into major U.S. broadcasters, which have broad free speech rights under the U.S. Constitution's First Amendment. Broadcast stations need FCC licenses to use public airwaves. While license revocations are extremely rare, critics say the threat of losing a license can pressure broadcasters and raise concerns about government interference in editorial and programming decisions.

item.title: Rays hope to continue small-ball success, aim to sweep visiting Padres
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays are the American League's top team, and they have arrived at the summit by running at will and putting pressure on their opponents.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Tampa Bay Rays are the American League's top team, and they have arrived at the summit by running at will and putting pressure on their opponents. The Rays will likely employ that same approach Sunday afternoon, probably with Chandler Simpson right in the thick of it, when the club goes for a series sweep against the San Diego Padres in St. Petersburg, Fla. The Rays lead baseball with a .261 team batting average and are sixth in stolen bases with 131, using a speedy approach instead of a slugging one that more resembles the high-speed Kansas City Royals and St. Louis Cardinals four decades ago, both of whom blazed the basepaths on their artificial turf. The 25-year-old Simpson, who delivered the game-winning RBI and had two hits in Saturday's 7-6 comeback victory, epitomizes that attacking, small-ball frenzy. In Friday's 9-4 win, he chopped a ball between first and second that rolled into shallow right field manned by San Diego's Fernando Tatis Jr. Simpson hustled out of the box and slid head-first into second for a double, willing to challenge Tatis' elite arm. He also stole two bases. The Atlanta native ranks third in AL hitting (.311). He is also third in stolen bases (37 of 51) and has a 90% contact rate. He is one of a few Rays who routinely bunts, even with the bases loaded. "We try to get runners over and get runners in," said Simpson, after his game-winner off tough lefty Adrian Morejon. "We just try to do our part to get everybody on base. ... I just trust in the work and the process and try to perfect my craft." Padres skipper Craig Stammen said the series opener was textbook Tampa Bay. "That's how they play: Steal bases, put pressure on you and make you play the defense in different spots to account for their speed and what they do with the bunt game," he said. "(When) they get a bunch of people on base, they're very tough to defend." On Saturday, the Padres blew a 6-3 lead after scoring three in the top half of the seventh. And it came at a cost. During Tampa Bay's four-run rally, second baseman Luis Rengifo was injured as his right leg collapsed on an awkward throw. He was then carted off the field. "It doesn't look good," Stammen said of the right knee, which was called a sprain and forced the club to send Rengifo back to southern California. The assignment of keeping the Rays off base Sunday and traffic to a minimum falls to San Diego's Ray - Robbie Ray (11-7, 3.21 ERA). This month has been a grind for the 34-year-old left-hander, who won 10 games for the San Francisco Giants before being traded down-state on Aug. 3. He is 1-1 with a 3.98 ERA in four starts with San Diego. Against Tampa Bay, Ray is 2-5 with a 3.21 ERA in 10 career starts. Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen (14-5, 2.95 ERA) has been dominant in August, winning all five of his outings and posting a 2.48 ERA. The right-hander, who has established a career-high in wins, has no record and a 6.00 in two relief appearances against San Diego. -Field Level Media

item.title: White Sox out to sweep Twins, quash division rival's faint playoff hopes
item.description: The Chicago White Sox and Minnesota Twins are headed in opposite directions.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago White Sox and Minnesota Twins are headed in opposite directions. The Twins have one game left in the series to try to make a U-turn. Chicago will look to complete a three-game sweep over Minnesota when the teams square off in the series finale Sunday afternoon in Minneapolis. The White Sox are coming off a 3-2 win on Saturday afternoon, which followed a 7-4 win in Friday's series opener. All told, the White Sox have won four games in a row and hold a 4 1/2-game lead for first place in the American League Central division. They are nine games over .500, the most on the season. Meanwhile, the Twins have lost four in a row and now sit eight games below .500. They are clinging to fading hopes of securing a wild-card playoff berth but have only 26 games to go. Minnesota started August a game above .500 and in second place in the Central, three games behind the White Sox in the division but holding the third and final American League wild card. An 8-17 record in August has sent the Twins plummeting to 8.5 games behind the White Sox and four games out of the wild card. "The vibes in here are completely fine," Twins second baseman Kody Clemens said after the game on Saturday. "Obviously, it's frustrating right now, given the game is just finished. But we've just got to continue to grind and get back to winning games." The White Sox have figured out that formula exceptionally well as of late. Andrew Benintendi has been a big reason for Chicago's success against the Twins this weekend. He went 2-for-4 with a double and two RBIs in Friday's series opener. On Saturday, he finished a triple shy of the cycle and had three hits and two RBIs. His three hits were the only three the White Sox had on the day. "I'm seeing it pretty well," Benintendi said. "Everybody on the field (and) off the field enjoys each other's company, and that always makes it better." White Sox manager Will Venable said Benintendi, who reached 10 years in the majors earlier this season, provides steady leadership at the plate. "Every one of our guys can learn from Benny and how he approaches it with runners in scoring position," Venable said. "It's about his experience. It's about his understanding of his own strengths. And he's been on the field in every type of situation that there is." Twins right-hander Zebby Matthews (8-8, 4.86 ERA) will try to help his team stave off the sweep. Matthews is set to make his 19th start of the season and the 44th of his brief career. The 26-year-old Matthews is red hot after winning each of his past four outings. His latest victory came against the Athletics, whom he held to one run on six hits in seven innings of a 9-6 road win on Monday. This will be Matthews' fourth career start against the White Sox. He is 0-1 with a 4.32 ERA in his first three outings, including a start on May 25 in which he took the 3-1 loss after allowing three runs on five hits in six innings. He walked one and struck out six. Chicago will counter with right-hander Jordan Hicks (2-1, 3.83), who will serve as the opener. Hicks has started 38 games in his career but only one this season. In three career appearances (one start) against the Twins, Hicks is 1-2 with a 6.14 ERA. Twins outfielder Walker Jenkins will aim for a strong finish to his first series in the big leagues. He singled in his debut on Friday night and notched his first career RBI on Saturday afternoon. -Field Level Media

item.title: Ducati's Marquez completes Aragon sweep to cut Martin's title lead
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez claimed his third straight victory at the Aragon Grand Prix on Sunday, reinforcing his superiority on anti-clockwise circuits as the reigning MotoGP champion closed the gap on championship leader Jorge Martin on home turf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez claimed his third straight victory at the Aragon Grand Prix on Sunday, reinforcing his superiority on anti-clockwise circuits as the reigning MotoGP champion closed the gap on championship leader Jorge Martin on home turf. Marquez's eighth triumph at MotorLand came after an intense battle with Aprilia's polesitter Marco Bezzecchi, whom he overtook in spectacular fashion on lap six as they went side-by-side at over 300 kph. KTM's Pedro Acosta finished second, extending his wait for a maiden MotoGP victory despite claiming his 14th podium finish, while Bezzecchi rounded out the top three and Alex Marquez finished fourth. Having won Saturday's sprint, Marquez claimed maximum points over the weekend to move up to 237, leapfrogging Bezzecchi (232) to climb to second behind Aprilia's Martin (256), who finished fifth. Bezzecchi had [USN:L4N44Q01W TEXT:"snatched pole position"] with a lap record but Marquez pounced on turn one to [USN:L1N44Q045 TEXT:"win the sprint"] , with the Spaniard attempting the same move in the race, only to see the Aprilia rider retake the lead at the next turn. 'HUGE MISTAKE' "The key point was the first corner. I did it again but I did a huge mistake today because I forgot the rear (ride-height) device and when I got from turn one to turn two, the rear device was activated and loaded again," Marquez said. "I was super slow on that fast turn two and three, two riders overtook me. Then, it was more difficult but from that point, I just built the pace." Marquez had to go on the offensive to reel in Bezzecchi, setting fastest laps as he set his sights on the Aprilia in front of him while Acosta stayed glued to his rear wheel in third. The reigning champion pounced on lap six, going alongside Bezzecchi on the back straight, riding mere inches apart and nearly making contact before overtaking the Aprilia. "I heard his bike on turn 15 so I tried to cross the line, but when we were close, the slipstream was pushing each other very much and it was strange," Bezzecchi said. "Marc, with the experience that he has and the speed that he has, today he was unbeatable." DELIGHT FOR HOME FANS Acosta also took the opportunity to move up to second at the next turn to hunt down Marquez, with the home fans roaring in delight as the two Spaniards then battled for the lead. But Marquez's consistency in setting fastest laps allowed him to put distance between him and Acosta, breaking the younger rider's resolve as the lead grew to over a second while Bezzecchi was nearly three seconds behind. Riding the wave of another Aragon triumph, Marquez hopped off his bike on the victory lap and hitched a ride to the stand named after him, sinking to his knees amid the deafening acclaim of supporters dressed in Ducati red.

item.title: Jamenei insta en un mensaje a gobernantes del golfo Pérsico a hacer frente al "verdadero enemigo"
item.description: El líder supremo de Irán, el ayatolá Mojtaba Jamenei, instó el domingo en un mensaje escrito a los gobernantes del golfo Pérsico a identificar a su "verdadero enemigo", comprender sus planes y hacerle frente.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El líder supremo de Irán, el ayatolá Mojtaba Jamenei, instó el domingo en un mensaje escrito a los gobernantes del golfo Pérsico a identificar a su "verdadero enemigo", comprender sus planes y hacerle frente. El mensaje, con motivo del aniversario del nacimiento del profeta Mahoma, publicado en la cuenta de Telegram de Jamenei, también hizo un llamado a la unidad, a la defensa mutua frente a los "enemigos" y a la cooperación entre los musulmanes de todo el mundo. No se ha visto a Jamenei en público desde que resultó herido en los ataques aéreos estadounidenses e israelíes de hace seis meses, que desencadenaron la guerra y en los que murió su padre y anterior líder supremo, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei.

item.title: Libya rivals agree roadmap for elections within 24 months at UN-led talks
item.description: Representatives of Libya's rival political parties on Sunday signed an agreement on holding long-delayed national elections within two years to resolve contentious issues over electoral laws and reform the national elections body.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Elumami
item.content:encoded: Representatives of Libya's rival political parties on Sunday signed an agreement on holding long-delayed national elections within two years to resolve contentious issues over electoral laws and reform the national elections body. The political process to resolve more than a decade of conflict in Libya has been stalled since an election scheduled for December 2021 collapsed following disputes over the eligibility of the main candidates. Sunday's signing ceremony was held at the United Nations Support Mission in Libya, UNSMIL, in the Libyan capital Tripoli. It followed talks in a smaller format, known as the 4+4, that involved two representatives of each of Libya's four main institutions: the Government of National Unity, the High Council of State, the House of Representatives and the Libyan National Army. Walid Ellafi, state minister of political affairs and communications in the Government of National Unity, said legislative and presidential elections should be held "within a period not exceeding 24 months" under a single executive authority and unified national institutions. Shibani AbuHamoud, head of the army's general command delegation, said the 4+4 would work with UNSMIL "to develop a framework within one month of the signing of the agreement to follow up on all matters related to its implementation". The agreement says that if Libya's House of Representatives and High Council of State fail to approve the deal within a month, the parties will seek to adopt it nationally as a constitutional document through broad national mechanisms and secure international backing through the U.N. Security Council. Libya has had little stability or security since a 2011 NATO-backed uprising. It split in 2014 between warring eastern and western factions but there has been little major warfare since a 2020 ceasefire. All Libya's major political players have repeatedly called for elections, but many Libyan people have voiced doubts that they would want a vote that could push most of them from positions of authority. (This story has been refiled to add the word 'delegation' in AbuHamoud's title in bullet point 5.)

item.title: Seven die, many more missing after ferry capsizes off North Cyprus
item.description: The privately owned ferry immediately started taking on water for an unknown reason after leaving port.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Seven die, many more missing after ferry capsizes off North Cyprus

The privately owned ferry immediately started taking on water for an unknown reason after leaving port.

A helicopter brings survivors ashore after they were rescued from the sea following a boat capsize off Kyrenia, northern Cyprus, on Aug 30, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Stringer)

NICOSIA: At least seven people died and 23 were missing after a ferry carrying around 270 passengers and crew capsized off North Cyprus on Sunday (Aug 30), leaving survivors clinging to its overturned hull. The privately owned ferry left the port of Kyrenia at 12.30pm and immediately started taking on water for an unknown reason, authorities said. It was heading for the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province in the eastern Mediterranean. The disaster occurred just off the coast of Kyrenia, a popular holiday resort for both locals and tourists. The ferry involved, a catamaran, was one of several shuttle sea services that link North Cyprus with Türkiye daily. Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman said 237 people had been rescued alive, while seven people had died and 23 people were still being sought.
